rows.question: How is a new o8 release shipped from a developer's machine? What is the exact local command sequence?
rows.referenceAnswer: npm version patch (bumps + tags via sync-version.mjs hook), then git push --follow-tags, then npm run ship (cargo tauri build with signing key + uploads via scripts/release.mjs to GitHub releases). Auto-update banner in installed app picks it up.

brain.text: A new patch release is shipped using the command sequence: `npm version patch && npm run ship` [FACT-99b1911f-1972-4566-ba58-20aef5003d01]. The project utilizes a signed Tauri release pipeline for shipping releases [FACT-d3a965c6-3a65-482d-b878-5713e6d9c78b].

grep.text: To ship a new o8 release from a developer's machine, the local command sequence is: `npm version patch`, `git push --follow-tags`, and `npm run ship` [CLAUDE.md:30,31,32,33]. This process bypasses CI and publishes to GitHub [CLAUDE.md:30]. The `npm version patch` command bumps the version and syncs manifests, while `npm run ship` builds and uploads the release [CLAUDE.md:31,33].

longCtx.text:
A new o8 release is shipped locally using the following command sequence:

1.  `npm version patch`
2.  `git push --follow-tags`
3.  `npm run ship`

This process bumps the version, syncs manifests, tags the commit, pushes to origin, builds a signed native app, and uploads it as a GitHub release. (CLAUDE.md - Shipping)

rows.question: Why is the Sonnet CLI timeout set to 300s in the composer Class B path?
rows.referenceAnswer: Sonnet CLI bootstrap can take 60-90s, then multi-row synthesis adds another 30-60s on the 30-row composer payload. The prior 60s default killed the call before the model even started generating, forcing fall-through to paid OpenRouter even when the user has a free Claude Max subscription. 300s lets the free CLI tier actually deliver.

rows.question: What does the daily compactor cron job do? What categories of work does it perform on the facts table?
rows.referenceAnswer: The compactor performs four jobs: (1) GC orphans (facts whose source rows are gone), (2) dedupe near-duplicate facts, (3) time-decay scoring of older facts, (4) near-dup merge into canonical facts. Runs daily via cron, scheduled per #915.

brain.text: The daily compactor cron job is responsible for transitioning dispatch rule entries from candidate status to either promoted or demoted [FACT-82cdeece-1409-4a94-9a6a-6fa3ff55229e]. This job represents the 'learned' part of the system and requires sufficient signal volume to validate its decisions [FACT-de57e7ae-e45d-420d-96f6-1de82cf9d917]. It is part of the Cursor Bugbot governance loop [FACT-18f8a2fa-f377-4fed-87aa-7fa06019b3a3].

rows.question: What was the ownership-category regression that prompted the rows.slice(0,20) → rows.slice(0,30) fix in src/lib/cortex/qa/composer.ts?
rows.referenceAnswer: Project rows from emitProjectRows landed at retrieval ranks 21-24 and got truncated by the slice(0,20). The retriever's unionMerge has MERGE_LIMIT=30, so the slice in the composer was tighter than the merge ceiling. Result: ownership accuracy stayed at 35% even after PR #949 paid the bill of adding project + project_repo retrieval. Matching the slice to MERGE_LIMIT=30 unlocked the project rows for the composer.
